text: An erDiagram with tables for schedules (linked to the existing tenants table), runs and per-attempt history, with key columns and relationships.
Explains how each fire time yields at most one run across several leaderless workers using only Postgres, with no broker or Redis.
States the overlap rule (a fire time during an in-progress run is recorded as skipped) and the missed-fire rule (only the most recent missed fire time runs).
Describes heartbeats every 30 seconds, takeover after 2 minutes without one, and that a worker presumed dead cannot overwrite the newer outcome.
Describes retries: at most 3 attempts, 1-minute then 5-minute waits, then failed, with a crash counting as an attempt.
Describes disable and pause: no new runs, executing runs finish, unstarted runs are cancelled, and no catch-up when a schedule is re-enabled or a tenant is resumed.
Covers tenant-visible run and attempt history, kept for 90 days, and how old history is removed.
Schedules store a cron expression and an IANA timezone, and fire times are computed in that timezone.
